items.name: Each State must give full faith and credit to other States' public acts, official
items.summary: Each State must give full faith and credit to other States' public acts, official records and judicial proceedings.

items.name: The text does not by itself establish identical enforcement of every sister-State
items.summary: The text does not by itself establish identical enforcement of every sister-State policy irrespective of subject, proceedings or controlling interpretation.

items.name: Congress may prescribe by general laws the manner of proof and effect of interstat
items.summary: Congress may prescribe by general laws the manner of proof and effect of interstate public acts, records and judicial proceedings.

items.name: Congressional standards for interstate recognition do not make State courts or leg
items.summary: Congressional standards for interstate recognition do not make State courts or legislatures federal agencies.

items.name: Article IV privileges and immunities protect citizens of each State in other State
items.summary: Article IV privileges and immunities protect citizens of each State in other States; do not silently substitute Fourteenth Amendment U.S.-citizen rights.

items.name: State interstate citizenship privileges and Fourteenth Amendment national privileg
items.summary: State interstate citizenship privileges and Fourteenth Amendment national privileges-or-immunities are textually distinct guarantees requiring different doctrinal tests.

items.name: Article IV extradition is triggered for a person charged in a State with treason,
items.summary: Article IV extradition is triggered for a person charged in a State with treason, felony or another crime who has fled from justice.

items.name: The charged fugitive must be found in another State before constitutional intersta
items.summary: The charged fugitive must be found in another State before constitutional interstate rendition provisions apply.

items.name: Demand originates from the executive authority of the State from which the charged
items.summary: Demand originates from the executive authority of the State from which the charged person fled.

items.name: Delivery is for removal to the State having jurisdiction of the charged crime, und
items.summary: Delivery is for removal to the State having jurisdiction of the charged crime, under constitutionally and statutorily applicable procedures.

items.name: Jurisdictional challenges, federal statutory procedures and judicial review of ext
items.summary: Jurisdictional challenges, federal statutory procedures and judicial review of extradition require a separate statute and case-law record.

items.name: Original Article IV interstate fugitive-service rendition rule is inoperative afte
items.summary: Original Article IV interstate fugitive-service rendition rule is inoperative after ratification of the Thirteenth Amendment.
items.note: Archive only; under no circumstances reconstruct a live claimant or enforcement duty.

items.name: No operative right to compel rendition of enslaved persons or claim their service
items.summary: No operative right to compel rendition of enslaved persons or claim their service may be derived from this original constitutional text.

items.name: Congress may admit new States into the Union.
items.summary: Congress may admit new States into the Union.

items.name: A State cannot be formed within another State or formed by joining two or more Sta
items.summary: A State cannot be formed within another State or formed by joining two or more States or their parts without consent of the legislatures of States concerned and Congress.

items.name: Federal legislation alone does not satisfy the express concerned State-legislature
items.summary: Federal legislation alone does not satisfy the express concerned State-legislature consents required for affected State division or merger.

items.name: Article IV grants Congress rules and disposal authority over territory or other pr
items.summary: Article IV grants Congress rules and disposal authority over territory or other property belonging to the United States.

items.name: The territorial and property clause must not prejudice the claims of the United St
items.summary: The territorial and property clause must not prejudice the claims of the United States or any particular State.

items.name: The text does not establish unlimited federal ownership of State property or elimi
items.summary: The text does not establish unlimited federal ownership of State property or eliminate all reserved State legal interests.

items.name: United States must guarantee a republican form of government to every State in the
items.summary: United States must guarantee a republican form of government to every State in the Union.

items.name: What constitutes a republican form of government, political question doctrine and
items.summary: What constitutes a republican form of government, political question doctrine and available remedies require separately verified judicial holdings.

items.name: United States shall protect each State against invasion; the express request prere
items.summary: United States shall protect each State against invasion; the express request prerequisite appears instead in the domestic-violence portion.

items.name: Federal protection must be evaluated with Article I congressional defense/appropri
items.summary: Federal protection must be evaluated with Article I congressional defense/appropriation powers and Article II commander-in-chief powers.

items.name: Federal domestic-violence protection requires application by the State legislature
items.summary: Federal domestic-violence protection requires application by the State legislature, absent the stated inability-to-convene alternative.

items.name: The State executive can apply for domestic-violence protection when the State legi
items.summary: The State executive can apply for domestic-violence protection when the State legislature cannot be convened.

items.name: This clause does not permit treating domestic-violence federal protection as havin
items.summary: This clause does not permit treating domestic-violence federal protection as having an unconditional Article IV trigger with no State application.

items.name: Debts and engagements contracted before the Constitution's adoption remain valid a
items.summary: Debts and engagements contracted before the Constitution's adoption remain valid against United States as they were under Confederation.

items.name: Original federal pre-Constitution obligations are distinct from Fourteenth Amendme
items.summary: Original federal pre-Constitution obligations are distinct from Fourteenth Amendment Section 4's protection of later lawfully authorized public debt.

items.name: The Constitution itself is part of the supreme law of the land and binds State jud
items.summary: The Constitution itself is part of the supreme law of the land and binds State judges.

items.name: Federal statutes have supremacy only when made in pursuance of the Constitution; t
items.summary: Federal statutes have supremacy only when made in pursuance of the Constitution; the clause does not independently enlarge Congress's enumerated powers.

items.name: Treaties receive the clause's priority where made under the authority of the Unite
items.summary: Treaties receive the clause's priority where made under the authority of the United States.

items.name: Judges in every State are bound despite contrary provisions of State constitutions
items.summary: Judges in every State are bound despite contrary provisions of State constitutions or laws.

items.name: Supremacy of valid federal law is not a general license for any federal officer or
items.summary: Supremacy of valid federal law is not a general license for any federal officer or agency to exercise powers absent authority from the Constitution and enacted law.

items.name: Any anti-commandeering limitation is a doctrine based on later constitutional inte
items.summary: Any anti-commandeering limitation is a doctrine based on later constitutional interpretation, not verbatim words of Article VI Clause 2.

items.name: Article VI requires Senators, Representatives, and federal executive and judicial
items.summary: Article VI requires Senators, Representatives, and federal executive and judicial officers to support the Constitution under oath or affirmation.

items.name: Article VI also requires State legislators and State executive and judicial office
items.summary: Article VI also requires State legislators and State executive and judicial officers to support the Constitution; the State is not converted into a federal agency.

items.name: No religious test may be required as qualification for any office or public trust
items.summary: No religious test may be required as qualification for any office or public trust under the United States.

items.name: Article VI's express religious-test clause concerns federal offices; prohibitions
items.summary: Article VI's express religious-test clause concerns federal offices; prohibitions applicable to State offices also involve First and Fourteenth Amendment jurisprudence.

items.name: Reservation applies to powers not delegated to United States AND not prohibited to
items.summary: Reservation applies to powers not delegated to United States AND not prohibited to States.

items.name: Reserved powers belong to States respectively or to the people, not a blanket tran
items.summary: Reserved powers belong to States respectively or to the people, not a blanket transferable federal administrative authority.

items.name: Reservation of nondelegated powers does not textually license unilateral State nul
items.summary: Reservation of nondelegated powers does not textually license unilateral State nullification of valid supreme federal law.

items.name: Tenth Amendment boundaries reinforce enumerated federal powers, but the exact dist
items.summary: Tenth Amendment boundaries reinforce enumerated federal powers, but the exact distribution and anti-commandeering doctrine require controlling precedent.

items.name: Express Eleventh Amendment wording concerns suits in law or equity commenced or pr
items.summary: Express Eleventh Amendment wording concerns suits in law or equity commenced or prosecuted against one of the States.

items.name: Express plaintiffs are citizens of another State and citizens/subjects of a foreig
items.summary: Express plaintiffs are citizens of another State and citizens/subjects of a foreign State, not every conceivable claimant.

items.name: Eleventh Amendment modifies the construction of Article III judicial power in spec
items.summary: Eleventh Amendment modifies the construction of Article III judicial power in specified suits against States.

items.name: Express Eleventh Amendment text is not a blanket prohibition on all cases involvin
items.summary: Express Eleventh Amendment text is not a blanket prohibition on all cases involving a State, including controversies between States.

items.name: Other doctrines of sovereign immunity extend beyond express Eleventh Amendment lan
items.summary: Other doctrines of sovereign immunity extend beyond express Eleventh Amendment language and require case-law-specific sourcing.

items.name: U.S. citizenship applies to persons born or naturalized in United States and subje
items.summary: U.S. citizenship applies to persons born or naturalized in United States and subject to its jurisdiction; the text's conditions are retained, not erased.

items.name: Citizens of the United States are also citizens of the State where they reside und
items.summary: Citizens of the United States are also citizens of the State where they reside under the Section 1 text.

items.name: Privileges or immunities under the U.S.-citizen clause are expressly rights of cit
items.summary: Privileges or immunities under the U.S.-citizen clause are expressly rights of citizens of the United States.

items.name: Fourteenth Amendment State due process protects any person, not only citizens, wit
items.summary: Fourteenth Amendment State due process protects any person, not only citizens, within its textually specified coverage.

items.name: Equal protection forbids a State from denying any person within its jurisdiction e
items.summary: Equal protection forbids a State from denying any person within its jurisdiction equal protection of the laws.

items.name: Section 1 rights restrictions are textually directed at States; federal due proces
items.summary: Section 1 rights restrictions are textually directed at States; federal due process is independently addressed in the Fifth Amendment.

items.name: Selective application of other Bill of Rights guarantees to States through Fourtee
items.summary: Selective application of other Bill of Rights guarantees to States through Fourteenth Amendment is a precedent-dependent doctrine, not automatic recitation of Section 1.

items.name: This architectural mapping does not adjudicate citizenship of any individual or co
items.summary: This architectural mapping does not adjudicate citizenship of any individual or conclusively resolve contested jurisdiction/status questions.

items.name: Section 2 describes House representation allocation among States by their respecti
items.summary: Section 2 describes House representation allocation among States by their respective populations subject to constitutional amendments.

items.name: Original Section 2 contains a reference to exclusion of 'Indians not taxed'; this
items.summary: Original Section 2 contains a reference to exclusion of 'Indians not taxed'; this historical constitutional language requires later legal context and must not serve as a current racial or tribal exclusion policy.
items.note: Not a freestanding valid contemporary exclusion from enumeration.

items.name: The original voting rights representation-reduction formulation uses a historical
items.summary: The original voting rights representation-reduction formulation uses a historical 21-year-old male voter reference; Twenty-Sixth Amendment changes the age-related constitutional reference.

items.name: Original Section 2 representation reduction includes a textual exception for parti
items.summary: Original Section 2 representation reduction includes a textual exception for participation in rebellion or other crime.

items.name: Historical Section 2 reduction mechanisms do not create an open-ended present Stat
items.summary: Historical Section 2 reduction mechanisms do not create an open-ended present State power to disenfranchise otherwise constitutionally protected voters.

items.name: Section 3 oath-based office disqualification only applies within its specified pri
items.summary: Section 3 oath-based office disqualification only applies within its specified prior-oath and covered-office categories.

items.name: Section 3 specifies engagement in insurrection/rebellion or aid and comfort to ene
items.summary: Section 3 specifies engagement in insurrection/rebellion or aid and comfort to enemies in relation to the Constitution.

items.name: The provision identifies specified federal and State offices; do not presume ident
items.summary: The provision identifies specified federal and State offices; do not presume identical treatment of every government or private position.

items.name: Congress may remove a Section 3 disability by two thirds vote of each House; a sim
items.summary: Congress may remove a Section 3 disability by two thirds vote of each House; a simple majority is not the textual standard.

items.name: Disqualification adjudication, enforcement procedures and contested terms require
items.summary: Disqualification adjudication, enforcement procedures and contested terms require controlling precedent; ARFI does not decide live candidates' eligibility.

items.name: The public debt protection refers to obligations of the United States authorized b
items.summary: The public debt protection refers to obligations of the United States authorized by law, including enumerated suppression of insurrection debts.

items.name: Neither federal nor State governments shall assume or pay debts or obligations inc
items.summary: Neither federal nor State governments shall assume or pay debts or obligations incurred in aid of insurrection or rebellion against the United States.

items.name: Neither federal nor State governments may pay claims for loss or emancipation of a
items.summary: Neither federal nor State governments may pay claims for loss or emancipation of an enslaved person; specified claims are illegal and void.

items.name: Section 4's debt provisions do not displace legislative taxing/borrowing/appropria
items.summary: Section 4's debt provisions do not displace legislative taxing/borrowing/appropriations authorities or confer unilateral spending power on the executive.

items.name: Congress may enforce the provisions of the Fourteenth Amendment by appropriate leg
items.summary: Congress may enforce the provisions of the Fourteenth Amendment by appropriate legislation.

items.name: The text's appropriate-legislation authority is tethered to Fourteenth Amendment p
items.summary: The text's appropriate-legislation authority is tethered to Fourteenth Amendment protections, not a blanket transfer of all State police power.

items.name: Proportionality, congruence and other limits on Section 5 laws require authoritati
items.summary: Proportionality, congruence and other limits on Section 5 laws require authoritative case-law records, not citation to text alone.
